schemes.name: CGTMSE
schemes.full: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro & Small Enterprises
schemes.oneLiner: Collateral-free business loans, government-guaranteed so banks lend without security.
schemes.quantum: Collateral-free credit; guarantee cover on loans up to the prevailing scheme ceiling (historically ₹2 Cr, since raised — confirm current cap with your lender).
schemes.guaranteeNote: Guarantee cover typically ranges ~75%–85% of the credit facility depending on loan size and borrower category; cover and ceilings are revised periodically by the Trust.
schemes.eligibleQuick: New or existing Micro/Small Enterprise in manufacturing or services, with Udyam registration, borrowing from an empanelled lender.
schemes.whoFor: New and existing Micro & Small Enterprises in manufacturing or services that lack collateral to pledge for a bank loan.
eligibility: Classified as a Micro or Small Enterprise under the MSMED Act (plant & machinery / equipment investment and annual turnover)
Business in manufacturing or services — trading-only units generally excluded (check if you straddle both)
Valid Udyam Registration
Clean repayment history; good credit score preferred
Loan from a lender empanelled as a Member Lending Institution (MLI) with CGTMSE
Loan must not already carry another government guarantee
howToApply: Prepare your business plan and project report
Approach a bank or NBFC empanelled as a CGTMSE Member Lending Institution
Submit the loan application; the lender assesses eligibility
On sanction, lender obtains CGTMSE guarantee cover and disburses the collateral-free loan
faqs: Is CGTMSE a loan or a guarantee?
CGTMSE itself doesn't lend — it guarantees the lender, so banks extend you a collateral-free loan with reduced risk.
What does the guarantee fee cost?
Lenders pass on an Annual Guarantee Fee (a small percentage of the loan, revised periodically). Confirm the current rate with your bank.
Are trading businesses covered?
Generally no — manufacturing and services are the core. If your business straddles both, check with your lender.
schemes.advisorAngle: Not every lender is an empanelled MLI, and the guarantee cover, ceilings, and annual guarantee fee change with circulars. We confirm the current cap, identify which local lenders actually process CGTMSE-backed loans, and structure the application so it qualifies.

schemes.name: PMEGP
schemes.body: Ministry of MSME via KVIC / KVIB / DICs
schemes.oneLiner: A margin-money subsidy that funds part of a brand-new micro-enterprise — money you don't repay if the unit runs through its lock-in.
schemes.quantum: Margin-money subsidy of 15%–35% of project cost. Project cost ceiling: up to ₹25 lakh (manufacturing) / ₹10 lakh (service) — some current guidelines reference higher project ceilings; confirm latest.
schemes.guaranteeNote: Subsidy depends on category and location: general 15% (urban) / 25% (rural); special category (SC/ST/OBC/women/minority/differently-abled/ex-servicemen) 25% (urban) / 35% (rural). Credited to the loan account and adjusted against the loan.
schemes.eligibleQuick: First-time entrepreneur, 18+, starting a NEW manufacturing or service unit. Existing or already-subsidised units don't qualify.
schemes.whoFor: First-time entrepreneurs (18+) starting a NEW manufacturing or service micro-enterprise. Existing or already-subsidised units are not eligible.
eligibility: Applicant aged 18 or above (no upper age limit)
For projects above the threshold, at least 8th-standard pass
Only NEW projects — expansion of an existing business does not qualify
No income ceiling — open to any income background
Individuals, SHGs, registered societies, cooperative societies and charitable trusts may apply
Udyam registration required before physical verification / margin-money adjustment
documents: Caste / special-category certificate (for enhanced subsidy, if applicable)
Machinery quotations and bank account details
howToApply: Prepare a strong, realistic Detailed Project Report (the #1 factor at sanction)
Apply online on the official PMEGP portal
Implementing agency (KVIC/KVIB/DIC) reviews and forwards to the bank
Interview / appraisal, then bank sanction and disbursement; subsidy adjusted into loan account
Track status via applicant login on the PMEGP portal
faqs: Can an existing business apply?
No — PMEGP is strictly for new units. Expansion of an existing business is handled under a separate second-loan window, not the core scheme.
Do I have to repay the subsidy?
The margin-money subsidy is adjusted into your loan and is retained if the unit runs through its lock-in period. Confirm the current lock-in with the implementing agency.
Should I pay an agent who guarantees approval?
No. The official portal explicitly warns against middlemen. Approval depends on a bankable project report, not a fixer.
schemes.advisorAngle: A weak or unrealistic project report is the most common cause of rejection, and the official portal warns against middlemen who 'guarantee approval.' We build a bankable DPR, ensure sector and category rules maximise your subsidy band, and shepherd the file through the DIC and bank stages.

schemes.name: CLCSS
schemes.oneLiner: A capital subsidy that pays back part of what you spend upgrading plant and machinery to better technology.
schemes.quantum: 15% capital subsidy on institutional credit for technology upgradation, on eligible plant & machinery investment up to ₹1 crore (subsidy ceiling and eligible sub-sectors are notified — confirm current list).
schemes.guaranteeNote: CLCSS supports upgrading to approved, better technology in notified sub-sectors. It is a capital subsidy on the machinery cost, routed through the lending bank.
schemes.eligibleQuick: Existing MSME upgrading to approved technology in a notified sub-sector, taking institutional credit for the machinery.
schemes.whoFor: Existing micro and small manufacturing enterprises upgrading to modern, approved technology in one of the notified sub-sectors.
eligibility: Existing MSME in manufacturing (the scheme targets technology upgradation, not greenfield)
Investment in approved/better technology within a notified sub-sector/product
Financing through institutional credit (a term loan from a participating bank/FI)
Valid Udyam registration
Machinery must meet the scheme's approved-technology criteria
documents: Term loan sanction from the financing bank
Machinery invoices / quotations meeting approved-technology criteria
howToApply: Confirm your upgrade falls in a notified CLCSS sub-sector with approved technology
Arrange a term loan for the machinery from a participating bank/FI
Apply for the capital subsidy through the bank, which routes it to the nodal agency
Subsidy is credited against the loan once approved
faqs: Can a new business use CLCSS?
No — CLCSS is for upgradation by existing units, not for setting up a brand-new unit. New units look to PMEGP or CGTMSE-backed credit.
Does my machinery qualify?
Only technology in the scheme's notified sub-sectors and approved-technology list qualifies. This is exactly where applications fail — verify before you buy.
schemes.advisorAngle: The scheme only covers approved technology in notified sub-sectors, and applications routinely fail because the machinery purchased doesn't match the approved list. We confirm your upgrade qualifies before you commit capital, and route the subsidy claim correctly through the bank and nodal agency.

schemes.name: PM Mudra Yojana
schemes.oneLiner: Collateral-free, guarantor-free micro-loans on a ladder from ₹50,000 to ₹20 lakh — built to fund the unfunded.
schemes.quantum: Collateral-free loans on four tiers: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001–₹5L), Tarun (₹5L–₹10L), and Tarun Plus (₹10L–₹20L, introduced via Budget 2024-25 for those who repaid a prior Tarun loan).
schemes.guaranteeNote: No direct subsidy under core PMMY; interest is bank MCLR-based, not a fixed government rate. A 2% interest subvention applied to Shishu loans for prompt repayment in some windows — confirm current. Loans are collateral-free and guarantor-free.
schemes.eligibleQuick: Any 18+ individual or micro-enterprise with a viable business plan in manufacturing, trading, services or allied-agri. Not for direct crop agriculture or large corporates.
schemes.whoFor: Non-corporate, non-farm micro and small enterprises — manufacturing, trading, services, and allied agricultural activities (dairy, poultry, food processing). New and existing both.
eligibility: Applicant typically 18–65
A viable business plan or an existing small business
Business in manufacturing, trading, services, or allied-agri (not direct crop/farm loans)
CIBIL score not mandatory for Shishu; 650+ generally preferred for Kishore/Tarun
Tarun Plus specifically requires prior successful repayment of a Tarun loan
documents: Business plan or quotation for the funding purpose
Category/proof documents as the lender requires
howToApply: Pick the tier (Shishu/Kishore/Tarun/Tarun Plus) matching your funding need
Approach a MUDRA-approved bank, NBFC, RRB or MFI — or apply via the JanSamarth portal
Submit the application with business details and documents
Bank verifies documents and business plan; on approval funds are disbursed (a MUDRA card may be issued)
faqs: Is there a subsidy on Mudra?
Not directly under core PMMY. Relief comes via linked schemes (e.g. CLCSS) or limited interest-subvention windows. The core benefit is collateral-free access.
Do I need collateral or a guarantor?
No — Mudra loans are collateral-free and guarantor-free, which is the whole point of the scheme.
Is the ₹10 lakh limit still current?
The limit was raised to ₹20 lakh via the Tarun Plus tier (Budget 2024-25). Many older guides still say ₹10 lakh.
schemes.advisorAngle: The tier you apply under, and whether you route through a bank vs the JanSamarth portal, materially affects approval speed and terms. We match you to the right tier and lender, and structure the business plan so a collateral-free file actually clears.

schemes.name: Startup India Seed Fund
schemes.oneLiner: Early-stage seed capital for DPIIT-recognised startups — grants for validation, convertible/debt for scale.
schemes.quantum: Up to ₹20 lakh as a grant (non-dilutive) for proof-of-concept, prototype or product trials; up to ₹50 lakh as convertible debentures or debt for market entry, commercialisation or scaling.
schemes.guaranteeNote: SISFS is disbursed through DPIIT-approved incubators, not directly. The grant portion does not need repayment; the convertible portion must be repaid or converts to equity per terms.
schemes.eligibleQuick: DPIIT-recognised startup, incorporated within the eligibility window, with an innovative scalable idea — applying through an approved incubator.
schemes.whoFor: DPIIT-recognised startups in early stages needing seed capital to validate, prototype, or take a product to market without immediately raising equity.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup (recognition is a prerequisite)
Incorporated within the scheme's age window at application
An innovative product/service with a scalable business model
Not received more than a capped amount of prior monetary support under other central/state schemes (per scheme terms)
Application made to a DPIIT-approved incubator
documents: Founder details and the innovation narrative
howToApply: Get DPIIT recognition first (prerequisite)
Apply on the Startup India Seed Fund portal, selecting DPIIT-approved incubators
The incubator evaluates and, if selected, disburses in milestones
Use grant for validation/prototype; convertible/debt for scaling per the agreement
faqs: Do I repay the seed fund?
The grant (up to ₹20L) is non-dilutive and not repaid. The convertible portion (up to ₹50L) is repaid or converts to equity per terms.
Do I need DPIIT recognition first?
Yes — SISFS is only open to DPIIT-recognised startups, so recognition is step zero.
schemes.advisorAngle: SISFS is disbursed through approved incubators, each with its own selection bar, and the grant-vs-convertible split has real equity consequences. We get your DPIIT recognition in place, target the right incubators, and structure the ask to maximise the non-dilutive portion.

schemes.name: DPIIT Recognition + 80-IAC
schemes.full: Startup India — DPIIT Recognition & Section 80-IAC Tax Exemption
schemes.oneLiner: The free, ~72-hour recognition that unlocks the entire Startup India benefit stack — and the separate, far harder tax holiday underneath it.
schemes.quantum: DPIIT recognition: free, approved in ~1–14 days. Unlocks Section 80-IAC (100% income-tax exemption for 3 consecutive years out of the first 10), angel-tax relief, 80% patent fee rebate, 50% trademark rebate, self-certification under labour & environment laws, and Seed Fund / GeM access.
schemes.guaranteeNote: Critical distinction: DPIIT recognition is necessary but NOT sufficient for the 80-IAC tax holiday. 80-IAC is a separate Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) application, reviewed within ~120 days, historically approved for only a small fraction of recognised startups — the innovation narrative is the #1 rejection reason.
schemes.eligibleQuick: Pvt Ltd, LLP, Partnership or Cooperative — incorporated from April 2016, within the age/turnover caps, with a genuine innovation angle. Not sole proprietorships.
schemes.whoFor: Private Limited companies, LLPs, Partnership firms and (2026) Cooperative Societies — incorporated from April 2016, under the age and turnover caps, with a genuine innovation / scalability angle.
eligibility: Entity is Pvt Ltd, LLP, Partnership Firm or Cooperative Society (not a sole proprietorship)
Incorporated on or after 1 April 2016
Within the recognition age window and below the turnover cap per the current framework
Working on innovation/improvement of products/services, or a scalable, employment-generating model
For 80-IAC specifically: only Pvt Ltd and LLPs are eligible for the tax holiday
documents: A clear innovation note — problem, solution, technology, evidence, scalability
For 80-IAC: DPIIT certificate, financial statements, strong innovation narrative for the IMB
howToApply: Incorporate your entity (Pvt Ltd / LLP / Partnership / Cooperative)
Apply for DPIIT recognition online via NSWS or the Startup India portal — free, no government fee
Recognition certificate typically issued within days
Separately apply for Section 80-IAC to the Inter-Ministerial Board with financials and innovation narrative
IMB reviews (~120 days); if approved, claim the tax holiday in a profitable year within the first 10
faqs: Is DPIIT recognition the same as the tax holiday?
No — and this trips up most founders. Recognition is easy and fast; the 80-IAC tax holiday is a separate, IMB-reviewed application with a low historical approval rate.
Does it cost anything?
DPIIT recognition is genuinely free — zero government fee. Anyone charging a 'government fee' is not authorised.
Can a sole proprietor apply?
No. You need a Pvt Ltd, LLP, Partnership or Cooperative. Incorporate first.
schemes.advisorAngle: Most founders confuse DPIIT recognition with the 80-IAC tax holiday — recognition is the easy part; the tax exemption is IMB-reviewed with a low historical approval rate, and a generic innovation write-up is the top reason for rejection. We get recognition fast and, where it's worth pursuing, draft the 80-IAC narrative to the standard the IMB approves. Beware anyone charging a 'government fee' — recognition is free.

schemes.name: Aatmanirbhar Gujarat (MSME)
schemes.full: Aatmanirbhar Gujarat Scheme for Assistance to MSMEs
schemes.oneLiner: Gujarat's flagship MSME package — interest subsidy up to 7%, plus capital subsidy and net SGST reimbursement, all scaled by taluka category.
schemes.quantum: Interest subsidy of 5%–7% on the term loan (Cat 1: 7%, max ₹35L/yr, 7 yrs; Cat 2: 6%, max ₹30L/yr, 6 yrs; Cat 3 & Municipal Corp: 5%, max ₹25L/yr, 5 yrs), plus +1% for women / differently-abled / registered startups and a further +1% for entrepreneurs under 35. Micro manufacturing units also get a capital subsidy of 25%/20%/10% of the term loan (up to ₹35L/₹30L/₹10L by taluka). Manufacturing MSMEs additionally get net SGST reimbursement of 80%–100% for 10 years (up to 5%–7.5% of eligible FCI p.a.). The enterprise bears a minimum 2% interest itself.
schemes.guaranteeNote: All benefits scale by the taluka category where the unit is located (Cat 1 > Cat 2 > Cat 3 / Municipal Corporation areas). Figures are from Government Resolution No. MIS-102022-1271(1)-I(CH) dated 05/10/2022, the Aatmanirbhar Gujarat Scheme for MSMEs, operative 05/10/2022 to 04/10/2027.
schemes.eligibleQuick: Micro/Small/Medium manufacturing or eligible-service unit in Gujarat (P&M investment ≤ ₹50 Cr), taking a term loan for new fixed assets. Exact tier set by taluka category.
schemes.whoFor: Micro, small and medium enterprises setting up or expanding eligible manufacturing or service units in Gujarat (fixed capital investment in plant & machinery up to ₹50 crore), financing new fixed assets through institutional credit.
eligibility: MSME by P&M investment: Micro ≤ ₹1 Cr, Small ₹1–10 Cr, Medium ₹10–50 Cr
Eligible unit located in Gujarat with Udyam / Udyog Aadhaar or DPIIT registration
Investment in new fixed assets (building, new P&M, utilities) financed by a term loan — land, working capital and second-hand indigenous P&M excluded
Apply within 1 year of first loan disbursement, commencement of production, or GR date (whichever is later)
Service-sector units must be on the GR's eligible list, employ 10+ persons and hold GST registration
Benefit tier determined by enterprise size and taluka category

howToApply: Confirm your unit, investment and taluka category under the Aatmanirbhar Gujarat MSME GR (05/10/2022)
Arrange the term loan for eligible new fixed assets
Apply through the Gujarat industries portal / District Industries Centre within the 1-year window
Obtain the Eligibility Certificate; claim interest subsidy, capital subsidy and net SGST reimbursement per sanctioned terms
faqs: Does the benefit depend on where in Gujarat I set up?

Yes — every component (interest subsidy, capital subsidy, net SGST) is tiered by taluka category, so location materially changes the subsidy. Category 1 talukas get the highest benefits. This is exactly where local advice pays off.
Can I stack this with a central subsidy?

Partly — if you also claim a central interest subsidy, the combined benefit can't reduce your own interest burden below 2%. Capital subsidy from state and centre together can't exceed the loan disbursed.
Is the capital subsidy for all MSMEs?
No — the capital subsidy component is only for micro manufacturing units. Interest subsidy and net SGST cover micro, small and medium.
schemes.advisorAngle: Gujarat's MSME benefits stack three ways — interest subsidy, capital subsidy and net SGST reimbursement — and every one is tiered by taluka category, with tight 1-year application windows and central-stacking limits. The same investment yields very different returns depending on where and how it's structured. Our Gujarat desk confirms your category, maximises the stack (including the +1% additions), and files within the deadlines.

schemes.name: Gujarat Textile Policy 2024
schemes.full: Gujarat Textile Policy 2024 — Capital & Interest Subsidy
schemes.body: Industries & Mines Dept / Commissioner of Textiles, Gujarat
schemes.oneLiner: Capital subsidy of 10%–35% of investment plus a 5%–7% interest subsidy across the textile value chain — one of India's most generous textile packages.
schemes.quantum: Capital subsidy of 10%–35% of eligible fixed capital investment (eFCI), scaled by taluka category and activity, up to a maximum of around ₹100 crore. Credit-linked interest subsidy of 5%–7% of eFCI for 5–8 years, with reimbursement capped at 2%–3% of eFCI per annum by taluka. A power-tariff subsidy of ₹1 per unit, plus payroll assistance of ₹3,000–₹5,000/month per female worker and ₹2,000–₹3,000 per male worker for up to 5 years for labour-intensive units.
schemes.guaranteeNote: Figures are from the Gujarat Textile Policy 2024 (announced October 2024 by the Industries & Mines Department). The capital subsidy band and interest-subsidy cap vary by taluka category and by which activity group your unit falls in; confirm your segment's exact entitlement.
schemes.eligibleQuick: Textile unit in Gujarat in a covered activity (garments, technical textiles, weaving, knitting, dyeing/processing, MMF spinning from PSF/VSF), investing in eligible plant/machinery with institutional finance.
schemes.whoFor: Textile manufacturers in Gujarat across the covered value chain — garments/apparel/made-ups and technical textiles (Activity 1); weaving, knitting, dyeing & processing, texturizing, twisting, embroidery and MMF spinning from PSF/VSF (Activity 2). Cotton and synthetic filament yarn spinning are excluded.
eligibility: Textile-sector unit in Gujarat in a covered activity group
Investment in eligible plant & machinery within a covered segment (cotton / synthetic filament yarn spinning excluded)
Institutional term-loan financing for the project
New unit or existing unit undertaking expansion / diversification
Compliance with the 2024 policy's registration, employment and segment criteria
documents: Term loan sanction and machinery invoices
Employment records (for payroll assistance / labour-intensive benefits)
howToApply: Confirm your activity group and machinery are covered under the Textile Policy 2024
Arrange eligible term-loan financing
Apply through the Commissioner of Textiles / Gujarat industries portal
Claim capital subsidy, interest subsidy, power-tariff and payroll assistance per sanctioned terms
faqs: Which textile segments are covered?

Two activity groups: (1) garments, apparel, made-ups and technical textiles; (2) weaving, knitting, dyeing & processing, texturizing, twisting, embroidery and MMF spinning from PSF/VSF. Cotton and synthetic filament yarn spinning are specifically excluded.
How much of my machine cost comes back?

Industry estimates put total recovery at roughly 25%–40% of machine cost once capital subsidy, interest subsidy and power benefits are combined — but it depends on taluka and activity. We model it for your specific case.
Is there help for labour-heavy units?
Yes — payroll assistance per worker (higher for women) and a separate fiscal-incentive track for labour-intensive units with very large headcounts.
schemes.advisorAngle: The 2024 policy is generous — 25%–40% of machine cost can come back across capital subsidy, interest subsidy and power benefits — but entitlement swings hard on activity classification and taluka, and the Surat belt routinely mis-classifies segments. Our Gujarat desk confirms current coverage and structures the claim across the whole value chain.

schemes.name: Gujarat Large Industry Incentive
schemes.full: Aatmanirbhar Gujarat Scheme for Large Industries & Thrust Sectors
schemes.oneLiner: For projects investing above ₹50 crore — net SGST reimbursement up to 100% for 10 years, plus a 7% interest subsidy, scaled by taluka and sector.

Interest subsidy at 7% on the term loan, capped at 1%–1.2% of eFCI per annum for 6–10 years by sector and taluka. EPF reimbursement up to ₹1,800/employee/month for 10 years, plus electricity-duty exemption for 5 years. The unit bears a minimum 2% interest itself.
schemes.guaranteeNote: This is the Large Industries & Thrust Sector arm of the Aatmanirbhar Gujarat Scheme — Government Resolution dated 05/10/2022, operative to 04/10/2027 — for manufacturers with fixed capital investment in plant & machinery above ₹50 crore. (MSMEs below that threshold fall under the Aatmanirbhar Gujarat MSME scheme.) Mega Industries (very large investment + high employment) have a separate enhanced tier.

schemes.whoFor: Large manufacturing projects in Gujarat with fixed capital investment in plant & machinery above ₹50 crore — new units or existing units undertaking expansion / diversification. Thrust-sector projects get enhanced terms.

faqs: How much does taluka location matter?

Significantly — net SGST (80%–100%) and the per-annum eFCI caps (5%–8%) both scale by taluka category, and Thrust-sector status raises them further. Over a 10-year window this is worth crores. Site selection is a strategic incentive decision.
Is this a separate scheme from the MSME one?
Same umbrella policy (Aatmanirbhar Gujarat 2022, GR 05/10/2022), split by size: above ₹50 Cr P&M = large/thrust arm; at or below = MSME arm. The two are filed differently.
What counts as a Thrust Sector?
The GR lists specific priority manufacturing sectors that receive higher SGST caps and shorter qualifying periods. We confirm whether your product qualifies.
schemes.advisorAngle: For a ₹50 Cr+ project the gap between taluka categories — and between General and Thrust classification — is worth crores over the 10-year SGST window, and the reimbursement mechanics (net SGST paid in cash, eFCI caps, Eligibility Certificates) are intricate. Our Gujarat desk models the incentive by location and sector and structures the application around the threshold and employment conditions.

schemes.name: Gujarat Startup Scheme
schemes.full: Gujarat Scheme for Assistance to Startups / Innovation
schemes.oneLiner: ₹20,000/month sustenance plus seed support up to ₹30 lakh, mentorship and accelerator funding for Gujarat-based startups.
schemes.quantum: Monthly sustenance allowance of ₹20,000 for one year (₹25,000 if the startup has at least one woman co-founder). Seed/product-development support up to ₹30 lakh for prototyping, raw materials, testing, market research and marketing. Up to ₹3 lakh to attend recognised national/international accelerator programs, up to ₹1 lakh for skill/managerial training, and up to ₹10 lakh extra for startups with significant social impact. A 1% additional interest subsidy (up to a 9% maximum on eligible term loans) under the MSME provisions, plus access to ₹50 lakh–₹3 crore mid-stage funding via Gujarat Venture Finance Ltd (GVFL).
schemes.guaranteeNote: Delivered through approved nodal institutions / incubators in Gujarat, with the screening committee approving each project. Amounts are from the current Gujarat startup assistance scheme (Industries Commissionerate). A startup can't simultaneously draw another state/central startup grant for the same project, though SSIP beneficiaries remain eligible.

faqs: How much is the sustenance allowance?
₹20,000 per month for one year per startup — or ₹25,000 per month if the startup has at least one woman co-founder.
Is the seed support a single grant?

No — the headline figure is cumulative across components (prototype/product development, accelerator, training, social impact). The ₹20,000/month sustenance is separate from the seed support. We map which components you can stack.
Can I combine this with central Startup India benefits?

Generally you can't draw two startup grants for the same project, but SSIP beneficiaries are exempted and central DPIIT recognition still applies. The sequencing matters — verify before assuming both.
schemes.advisorAngle: Founders routinely confuse the ₹20,000/month sustenance with the seed grant, and miss that the headline support is cumulative across components with anti-double-dipping rules against other startup grants. Our Gujarat desk routes you to the right nodal institution, sequences state and central benefits correctly, and stacks the components you're actually eligible for.
